status: 72-game grouped validation complete; prospective forecasts and outcomes pending
summary: Payoffs predict behavior, but much of the learned improvement is explained by basic payoff-to-action mapping, game-family regularities, and equilibrium selection. Generalization across complete families remains weak for cooperation. Learning provides some probabilistic improvements on supported domains; the prospective test is still pending.
findings: The fixed dataset has 1,918 valid eight-round matches over 72 game shapes and four models. Development completed 960/960 matches; the pilot completed 958/960. Trace and protocol audits passed.

On family holdouts, combined-logistic Brier is 0.173 for action choice, 0.302 for mutual cooperation, and 0.159 for coordination, versus ordered-context means 0.252, 0.316, and 0.221. The cooperation gain has an interval crossing zero. Held-out Prisoner’s Dilemma cooperation Brier is 0.901.

A secondary equilibrium selector designed after the pilot achieves family-held-out Brier 0.151, 0.084, and 0.146 for the same targets. Learned action/cooperation Brier is worse, with descriptive paired intervals excluding zero; coordination is inconclusive. These are post-pilot retrospective sensitivity results, separate from the original methods.

Learned action log loss is lower than the secondary equilibrium rule (0.558 versus 0.810), paired improvement 0.252 [0.054, 0.491]. Coordination log-loss improvement 0.081 has interval [-0.002, 0.174]. Avoiding extreme zero/one errors does not establish superior calibration everywhere or rule out a simple softened theory baseline, which was not tested.

On random game splits, the fixed family average nearly matches learned mutual-cooperation Brier (0.0740 versus 0.0746) and coordination (0.1359 versus 0.1373). Action0 requires payoff-to-encoded-action information because the generator reverses action encoding; gains need not imply nuanced within-family strategy prediction.

Focal/opponent identities add little to action prediction: random-group game-only versus both-ID combined logistic scores 0.1462 versus 0.1465. Known-shape model/pair success supports a shared payoff response more directly than individualized behavioral traits.

Global parameter-region extrapolation still fails for combined-logistic action Brier (0.340 versus context 0.257), while coordination improves to 0.256 versus original Nash 0.257. This test changes family composition: the larger training subset contains two Chicken games whereas the pilot contained none. It is not a controlled within-family parameter change.

Balanced pilot label swaps shift canonical action choice most in equal-payoff coordination games. Aggregate cooperation/coordination differences have intervals crossing zero; this is not an equivalence test. Conditional forgiveness has only 552 opportunities in the larger dataset and no consistent predictive gain.

Conditional Brier gains can depend on training-objective weights. On family-held-out exploitation, the event-weighted context baseline scores 0.262 versus combined logistic 0.285, reversing its apparent gain over the original context baseline (0.308). This does not establish a robust predictor of payoff-extraction behavior.

Grouped validations are separate from prospective evidence. All secondary future forecasts were frozen at 07:19:57 UTC before prospective/control play. The numerical and prompted primary forecasts will also finish before the 21 new game shapes are played. These shapes come from the same seven archetypes; no eighth-family claim or Gate 8 experiment is included.
